evidence: The six dependency-free evaluation modules and their integration passed 107 targeted and existing evaluation regression tests.
Ruff lint and format checks passed for all new evaluation modules and tests.

An independent code-review pass found four acceptance, articulation-window, small-image, and time-normalization defects; all four were fixed, covered by regressions, and confirmed resolved in a second review.
The full repository test suite remains blocked during collection by the pre-existing missing module phiagent.rendering.minimax_h3 in tests/test_acwm_hand_structure.py.
lessons: A fail-closed metric stack also requires the experiment summary to preserve the exact contract used for each per-unit decision.
Motion smoothness must declare both timestamp units and a dimensionally compatible jerk normalization.
Synthetic negative controls are useful engineering evidence but do not establish real-scene physical-transfer validity.
limitations: The complete contract has not been run on frozen real evaluation units with robot masks, landmarks, calibrated object tracks, EPL phases, and contact evidence.
The deterministic sharpness and pixel-temporal diagnostics are proxies, not perceptual-realism or physical-execution metrics.
next_actions: Freeze independent real scene-action-object-embodiment-seed units, generate the required structured observations with pinned perception adapters, and report VTR with Wilson intervals and worst-group rates.
Resolve the unrelated phiagent.rendering.minimax_h3 collection blocker before claiming a clean full-repository test run.
scope: Strict physical-transfer evaluation contract and synthetic CPU validation
summary: Implemented and regression-tested strict action, EPL, embodiment, interaction, temporal, background, and experiment-level VTR evaluation, but complete real-input acceptance remains not run.
